name: Elon Musk
title: The Boy Who Bet on Mars
subtitle: From a $500 video game in Pretoria to rockets, electric cars and the world's biggest fortune, and what it all cost him.
hook: In December 2008, both of Elon Musk's companies were close to death. On 23 December, NASA picked SpaceX, whose Falcon 9 rocket had ==never flown a full mission==, for up to **$1.6 billion** of space-station cargo flights. The next evening, at ==6 pm on Christmas Eve==, Tesla's rescue funding round finally closed. Musk later wrote that it was the "Last hour of last day possible", with the company three days from bankruptcy.

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Pretoria, with a South African father and a Canadian mother. At 12 he sold the code for his space game Blastar to a magazine for $500.

glance.label: Left home
glance.value: Moved to Canada alone at 17 and worked on a cousin's farm in Saskatchewan

glance.label: Toughest early job
glance.value: Cleaning out a lumber-mill boiler room in Vancouver for $18 an hour

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Two years at Queen's University, Canada, then the University of Pennsylvania: physics plus an economics/business degree from Wharton, dated 1997

glance.label: First company
glance.value: Zip2 (1995, age 24, with brother Kimbal): online maps and directories for newspapers. Sold to Compaq in 1999 for $307 million.

glance.label: Second company
glance.value: X.com (1999), which became PayPal. eBay bought PayPal for about $1.5 billion in stock in 2002.

glance.label: Runs today
glance.value: CEO of Tesla and of SpaceX. SpaceX absorbed xAI (which owns X) in February 2026 and listed on Nasdaq in June 2026 in a record $75 billion IPO.

glance.label: Net worth
glance.value: About $924 billion (Forbes real-time, 29 Oct 2026), the richest person on Forbes's list. Forbes briefly had him above $1 trillion on 9 Oct 2026.

glance.label: Family & home
glance.value: Divorced; father of 14 children, per Forbes. Lives in Austin, Texas.

contact.howToReach: Musk's only personal public channel is his X account, @elonmusk, where he posts constantly and sometimes replies in public, but with an audience that size a cold DM almost never gets read. Classic press routes are close to dead too: Tesla disbanded its US PR team in 2020, and X's press inbox once auto-replied to journalists with a poop emoji. What does work is going to the right team for the right reason: investor questions to Tesla Investor Relations or SpaceX's corporate secretary, media questions to SpaceX's media desk, and jobs through hiring calls Musk posts himself, such as the August 2026 request for a résumé plus three bullet points of exceptional ability sent to datacenters@spacex.com. The Musk Foundation's website lists its focus areas but publishes no application process, so don't send grant pitches, and never pay a "contact finder" site or trust anyone who claims to be Musk and asks for money or crypto. Keep any message under 150 words: one line on who you are, three concrete bullets on what you have actually built, and one clear ask.

factCheck.method: Front matter and contact card built from primary records first: Tesla's FY2025 10-K and October 2026 proxy statement (SEC EDGAR), SpaceX's June 2026 S-1/A and its investor-relations pages, PayPal's 2002 SEC filing on the eBay deal, NASA JPL's press-kit contact list, and the companies' own websites. Biography facts were cross-checked against Britannica, Queen's University and Wharton publications, and established press (CNBC, Fortune, Spaceflight Now, Euronews). The hook's Christmas 2008 timing uses Spaceflight Now's same-day report and Musk's own post. Net worth is the Forbes real-time figure read on 29 Oct 2026. Photos and licences were read from the Wikimedia Commons API (imageinfo/extmetadata); thumbnails use the standard 960px size because Commons now rejects a 1000px width. Socials cite the official profiles themselves; no personal contacts, guessed emails or data-broker sites were used.

disputed.claim: Year Musk left South Africa for Canada
disputed.note: Britannica says 1988; Queen's Alumni Review gives inconsistent years (1989–91 and 1990), and many accounts say June 1989, just before he turned 18. All agree he was 17, which is what we state.

disputed.claim: Musk enrolled at Stanford for two days in 1995
disputed.note: Musk's long-told story (repeated by Britannica) is that he left a Stanford graduate programme after two days. In October 2024 the Washington Post reported he never took classes, and Stanford told CNN it had no record he enrolled, though he had been admitted to its materials science programme. We do not list Stanford in Education.

disputed.claim: Name of Musk's second Penn degree
disputed.note: Often given as a BS in economics from Wharton; Knowledge at Wharton calls it an undergraduate business degree. Penn dates both degrees to 1997, though he left campus in 1995. We say 'economics/business degree from Wharton'.

disputed.claim: How many workers quit the boiler-room job
disputed.note: CNBC (citing Ashlee Vance's biography) says 30 started and only three were left by the end of the week; other retellings say two of 30. We leave the number out.
SpaceX's S-1/A filed with the SEC gives Starbase, Texas 78521; its IR contact page printed 78725 (Tesla's Austin ZIP) when checked on 29 Oct 2026, likely a typo. We use the SEC filing.

Forbes put him above $1 trillion on 9 Oct 2026 and the Daily Pennsylvanian called him the first trillionaire after the June 2026 SpaceX IPO, but Forbes's real-time figure was $977.2 billion on 13 Oct and $924 billion on 29 Oct 2026. The figure moves with SpaceX and Tesla shares, so we give the dated Forbes number.

disputed.claim: Musk's SpaceX ownership after the IPO
disputed.note: Fortune (Oct 2026) says about 45% of shares and about 82% of votes; some IPO-day coverage said 49%. Not stated in our glance.
